title: Malware and Social Engineering
intro: An independent 10–15 minute catch-up with feedback, unlimited retries and 80% mastery.

options: Software designed to harm or compromise systems
questions.answer: Software designed to harm or compromise systems
questions.feedback: Malware includes many forms of malicious software.

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read and follow the new material.

blocks.title: Malware harms systems
blocks.text: Malware is software designed to harm, disrupt or gain unauthorised access to systems. Different malware types have different behaviours.

blocks.title: Trojan, worm and ransomware
blocks.text: A trojan disguises itself as legitimate software; worms replicate to spread; ransomware may encrypt files and demand payment.

blocks.title: Social engineering
blocks.text: Attackers deceive people into sharing information or taking an unsafe action. A phishing message impersonates a trusted organisation.

blocks.title: Look for warning signs
blocks.text: Unexpected links, urgency and requests for account details are warning signs. Know the threat and explain why sharing credentials is dangerous.

blocks.title: Worked example
blocks.text: The sender pretends to be a trusted school service. This is phishing/social engineering [1]: the pupil is directed to a fake page or asked for details [1]. The attacker may capture login credentials [1] and gain unauthorised access to the pupil's account [1]. Name the threat, describe the deception and link data theft to access.

items: Malware — Malicious software that harms or compromises systems.
Trojan — Malware disguised as trustworthy software.
Worm — Malware able to replicate and spread to other systems.
Ransomware — Malware that can lock or encrypt data and demand payment.
Social engineering — Manipulating people to reveal information or take risky actions.
Phishing — Deceptive messages seeking personal or account information.
Pharming — Redirecting users to a fraudulent website.
Shoulder surfing — Watching someone enter secret information.
